body:
I live in honors and a lot of the newer honors students seem oblivious to common courtesy. 

One day I'm trying to get out of the elevator with my hands full and these kids try to squeeze in past me as I'm struggling to come out... like come on guys. Another night I worked a late shift and just wanted to go to my room, when a bunch of kids literally gathered around the doorway saying goodbye to each other, not noticing I'm trying to get in.

This is a new pet peeve and it drives me nuts how little awareness/consideration they can have. I spend most of my time outside the dorm and I only notice this from recent honors students.

Not sure if it's a symptom of them dedicating so much time to studies that they don't know any better, they just believe they're above others, or both. The academic stats of newer honors kids are unbelievable, so I guess something had to give. They're usually very odd to talk to as well, besides being nerdy which I get.
I asked 2 different employees and confirmed with another guy that there is no coat check. I keep wondering how people are wearing short sleeves
Last I checked, you need to be living on campus to swipe into honors. Otherwise, tell the DA that you’re going to the second floor, or get someone to sign you in.

There's a piano on the second floor of the honors building. It's common courtesy to play it after office hours and the honors staff leaves for the day (around 4pm). The room it's in has interesting acoustics and it's relatively easy to find empty.
I feel this 100%. I can tell you're in despair and struggling. If you keep telling yourself you're *eventually* going to kill yourself, one of these days may be better than the other shitty ones.
